3: import {
4:   motion,
5:   useMotionValue,
6:   useReducedMotion,
7:   useSpring,
8: } from "framer-motion";
9: import type { PointerEvent, ReactNode } from "react";
10: 
11: import { SPRING_MOUSE } from "@/lib/ease";
12: import { useHoverCapable } from "@/lib/hooks/use-hover-capable";
13: import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
14: 
15: export interface MagneticProps {
16:   children: ReactNode;
17:   className?: string;
18:   /** Fraction of the pointer distance the element travels toward the cursor (0-1). Default 0.35. */
19:   strength?: number;
20:   /** Maximum travel distance in px from the rest position. Default 32. */
21:   maxOffset?: number;
22:   /** Scale applied while the pointer is inside the element. Default 1.04. */
23:   hoverScale?: number;
24: }
25: 
26: const clamp = (value: number, min: number, max: number) =>
27:   Math.min(Math.max(value, min), max);
28: 
29: export const Magnetic = ({
30:   children,
31:   className,
32:   strength = 0.35,
33:   maxOffset = 32,
34:   hoverScale = 1.04,
35: }: MagneticProps) => {
36:   const reduce = useReducedMotion();
37:   const canHover = useHoverCapable();
38: 
39:   const offsetX = useMotionValue(0);
40:   const offsetY = useMotionValue(0);
41:   const x = useSpring(offsetX, SPRING_MOUSE);
42:   const y = useSpring(offsetY, SPRING_MOUSE);
43:   const scale = useSpring(1, { damping: 22, mass: 0.4, stiffness: 320 });
44: 
45:   const pull = (event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
46:     if (!canHover || reduce) {
47:       return;
48:     }
49:     const rect = event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();
50:     const dx = event.clientX - (rect.left + rect.width / 2);
51:     const dy = event.clientY - (rect.top + rect.height / 2);
52:     offsetX.set(clamp(dx * strength, -maxOffset, maxOffset));
53:     offsetY.set(clamp(dy * strength, -maxOffset, maxOffset));
54:   };
55: 
56:   const release = () => {
57:     offsetX.set(0);
58:     offsetY.set(0);
59:     scale.set(1);
60:   };
61: 
62:   return (
63:     <motion.div
64:       className={cn("inline-block", className)}
65:       style={{ scale, x, y }}
66:       onPointerEnter={() => {
67:         if (!canHover || reduce) {
68:           return;
69:         }
70:         scale.set(hoverScale);
71:       }}
72:       onPointerMove={pull}
73:       onPointerLeave={release}
74:       onPointerCancel={release}
75:     >
76:       {children}
77:     </motion.div>
78:   );
79: };
80: 
81: export default Magnetic;

input.content: --- title: Parallax Floating description: A wrapper that creates a parallax floating effect on cursor and touch movement. --- import { ParallaxFloatingDemo } from "@/demo/parallax-floating-demo"; ## Installation If you've already added the prsui registry, use the short command: Otherwise, use the full registry URL: ## Usage `Floating` is the wrapper that tracks the pointer and drives the animation. Wrap any element you want to float — images, videos, SVGs, cards — with `FloatingElement` and give it a `depth`: ```tsx import Floating, { FloatingElement } from "@/components/prsui/parallax-floating"; export function MyComponent() { return ( ); } ``` Elements with a higher `depth` travel further from the pointer, creating a parallax effect. The animation runs on `requestAnimationFrame` and eases each element toward its target, so it stays smooth even as elements are added or removed. Pointer tracking works with both mouse and touch. ## Props ### Floating | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Elements to float | | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes merged onto the wrapper | | `sensitivity` | `number` | `1` | Multiplier for how far elements travel | | `easingFactor` | `number` | `0.05` | Interpolation factor per frame toward the target (0-1)| ### FloatingElement | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ---------- | ------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The element that gets the floating effect | | `className`| `string` | - | Additional CSS classes merged onto the wrapper | | `depth` | `number` | `1` | How strongly this element reacts to the pointer |

content.text:
Done. Created the parallax floating component in the prsui registry:

- `registry/new-york/parallax-floating.tsx` — exports `Floating` (default, named `Floating`), the pointer-tracking wrapper with `sensitivity`/`easingFactor` props, and `FloatingElement` with a per-element `depth`. Works with any HTML (images, videos, SVGs) since it animates via `translate3d` on a `requestAnimationFrame` loop with eased interpolation. Touch + mouse both tracked.
- `lib/hooks/use-mouse-position-ref.ts` — ref-based pointer tracking (no re-render per move), derived from your `use-mouse-position` example.
- `demo/parallax-floating-demo.tsx` — demo with SVG/emoji/gradient elements at depths 0.6–3.
- `content/docs/components/floating.mdx` — docs page (matches the existing `floating` entry in `content/docs/components/meta.json`), with installation commands and props tables.
- `registry.json` — registered `parallax-floating` (deps: `motion`), shipping both the component and hook files.

All my files pass `typecheck`, lint (0 warnings), and formatting; the 3 remaining format failures (`link.mdx`, `logo-grid.mdx`, `theme-toggle.mdx`) pre-exist in files I didn't touch.
